visual_goal: Show that Oracle subledgers and external sources through Accounting Hub both pass through the same rules engine, whose detail stays in the subledger repository while General Ledger and the balances cube receive only what the chart of accounts can express.
prompt: A left-to-right flow diagram. At the far left, two plain server boxes stacked vertically: the upper one labeled 'Wayfare platforms', the lower one labeled 'Oracle subledgers'. One arrow from 'Wayfare platforms' into a box labeled 'Accounting Hub' to its right. Next, in the center, a large gear machine labeled 'Accounting rules' receiving one arrow from 'Accounting Hub' and one arrow from 'Oracle subledgers', so both sources enter the same machine. From the gear machine one arrow into a tall filing cabinet full of many detailed lines labeled 'Subledger repository'. From the cabinet, one arrow passes through a small funnel into an open book labeled 'General ledger'; only a few thick lines come out of the funnel, showing less detail. From the open book one arrow into a cube labeled 'Balances cube', and from the cube one arrow to a box at the far right labeled 'OneStream'. Below the cabinet, one arrow down from the cabinet to a box with a magnifying glass labeled 'Analytics'. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: External platforms through Accounting Hub and Oracle subledgers both feed one accounting rules engine; its detailed journals stay in the subledger repository, which feeds analytics, while a funnel passes summarized lines to the general ledger, the balances cube and OneStream.

visual_goal: Show the rail ticket's events travelling as files through an adapter into Accounting Hub, accounted by rules and summarized into General Ledger, with the ticket detail kept one drill-down away.
prompt: A left-to-right flow diagram. At the far left, a server box labeled 'Booking platform' with two small envelopes leaving it, one tagged '3 Mar' and one tagged '5 Mar'. One arrow from it into a box labeled 'Adapter' that has a green check mark. One arrow from the adapter into a small stack of file documents labeled 'Daily files'. One arrow from the files into a box with a gear labeled 'Accounting Hub'. Directly below Accounting Hub, a filing cabinet with many fine lines and a magnifying glass, labeled 'Ticket detail', with one arrow down from Accounting Hub into it. From Accounting Hub one arrow through a small funnel into an open book labeled 'General ledger'. A thin dotted line runs from the open book back down to the 'Ticket detail' cabinet, showing drill-down. From the open book one arrow labeled 'monthly' to a box at the far right labeled 'OneStream'.
alt: Ticket events dated 3 and 5 March leave the booking platform, pass an adapter check, travel as daily files into Accounting Hub, which keeps the ticket detail in a cabinet and sends summarized journals to the general ledger, with a dotted drill-down line back to the detail and a monthly feed to OneStream.

visual_goal: Show each Fusion integration surface doing one job: REST for low-volume inbound, FBDI for bulk inbound, business events as outbound notifications, Data Extraction for bulk outbound, and the ledger sending trial balances to consolidation.
prompt: A left-to-right diagram with three soft background panels. Left panel (light teal): two boxes stacked, 'MuleSoft' on top and 'Rail adapter' below. Center panel (light blue), a large building representing the Fusion tenant with four doors along its walls: a small door labeled 'REST', a wide loading-bay door labeled 'FBDI', a door with a lightning bolt labeled 'Business events', and a wide loading-bay door labeled 'Data Extraction'; inside the building an open book labeled 'General ledger'. Right panel (light orange): three boxes stacked, 'OneStream', 'BlackLine', 'FinDB'. Arrows: one thin arrow from 'MuleSoft' into the 'REST' door; one very thick arrow carrying a stack of files from 'Rail adapter' into the 'FBDI' loading bay; one thin lightning-bolt arrow from the 'Business events' door back left to 'MuleSoft'; one arrow from the 'General ledger' book to 'OneStream'; two thick arrows carrying stacks of files from the 'Data Extraction' loading bay, one to 'BlackLine' and one to 'FinDB'. Exactly six arrows.
alt: Inbound MuleSoft flows use the small REST door and the rail adapter's bulk files use the FBDI loading bay; business events notify MuleSoft; the general ledger feeds OneStream and the Data Extraction loading bay sends bulk extracts to BlackLine and FinDB.
